sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant has falsely been implicated in the present case.
It is further submitted that as per the prosecution case, victim was in live-in-relation with the appellant on her own, but thereafter, due to some misunderstanding, the F.I.R. was lodged.
It is vehemently submitted that later on, they solemnized marriage in a temple, but without considering all these facts, the Investigating Officer filed the charge sheet.
It is lastly submitted that the court below has not considered all these facts while rejecting the bail application and the trial is also not going on.
It is also submitted that as the charge sheet has been filed, there is no possibility of tampering of any evidence.
It is, thus, submitted that the impugned order is liable to be set aside and the appellant, who does not have any criminal antecedent and is in jail since 30.11.2023, is entitled for bail.
It is also submitted that the appellant is ready to cooperate in the trial.
5. Learned A.G.A. opposes the prayer of the appellant and submits that after detail investigation, the charge sheet has been file and there is no illegality in the impugned order.

6. However, learned counsel for the complainant, while conceding with the argument advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant, submits that the prosecutrix was residing with the appellant in live-in-relation.

It is also admitted by the learned counsel for the complainant that the marriage of the prosecutrix has been solemnized with the appellant in a temple and they are enjoying their matrimonial life and she does not want to prosecute the appellant.

7. Considering the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant, learned A.G.A.,
learned counsel for the complainant and going through the contents of the appeal, impugned order,
counter affidavit as well as other relevant documents, it is undisputed that the victim is a major lady and she was residing with the appellant in live-in-relation.

It is also evident from the contents of the short counter affidavit filed by the learned counsel for respondent no. 2 that the marriage of the prosecutrix has been solemnized with the appellant on 24.11.2023 in a temple.

8. In view of above facts and circumstances as also keeping in view the fact that the trial of the case is not likely to be concluded in near future, the appeal has substance and it is accordingly, allowed.
9.

Impugned order dated 14.12.2023 passed by Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Barabanki in Bail Application No. 5443 of 2023 arising out of F.I.R. No. 1198 of 2023, under Sections 376, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act, P.S. Kotwali Nagar, District Barabanki is hereby set aside.
10.

sentences.text: In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The appellant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through their counsel.

In case of his absence, without sufficient cause,
the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the appellant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence, proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation,
then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law,
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
(iv) The appellant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the appellant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
